title: Automated sample-weighted eval + per-field sensitivity alerts for JSON outputs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight continuous evaluation pipeline that detects quality regressions for JSON/structured outputs by combining sample-weighted metrics and per-field sensitivity tests, triggered on model or serving-config changes. Motivation: existing schema checks flag hard violations but miss subtle quality regressions (missing nested fields, shifted distributions for numeric/string enums, truncated arrays). We need automated, low-noise alerts tied to the specific config or model delta that caused the regression, with actionable per-field telemetry so engineers can triage quickly.

Scope: prototype an evaluation job that runs when (a) a model version is promoted to a rollout, (b) serving config changes (quantization, batching, kernel profile), or (c) canary traffic diverges beyond a threshold. The job will sample production-like prompts (sampled from recent traffic, weighted by frequency and business value) and compute per-field metrics (presence rate, token-length distribution, token-level edit distance on string fields, numeric drift via Wasserstein distance, enum-probability shifts). The pipeline should: 1) attach the eval run to the rollout/change metadata, 2) emit structured metrics to Console (per-route/per-field), 3) raise alerts with contextual diffs and suggested remediation (rollback, increase beam/temperature, pin older model).

Non-goals: exhaustive fuzz testing, human-in-the-loop judging at scale (this is an automated signal to augment, not replace, existing eval gates).
acceptance_criteria:
1) CI/automation runs an eval job when a model or config delta is recorded and produces a JSON summary file stored in the eval bucket.
2) Metrics emitted: per-field presence_change_pct, median_length_delta, enum_pmi_shift, string_levenshtein_rate, and an aggregate weighted_regression_score.
3) Alerts fire if weighted_regression_score > 0.12 OR any critical-field presence_change_pct > 0.15 for customer-facing fields.
4) Alert payload includes: the model/config diff id, top-3 regressing fields with metric deltas, example inputs+old_output+new_output (sanitized), and link to run artifacts.
5) Integration tests (unit + e2e) that validate the pipeline against a controlled regression dataset.
6) Documentation: README for the eval job, runbook for alerts, and Console dashboard facet for per-field trends.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: lightweight Python job (eval-service) that: 1) loads the change event (model_id, config_hash), 2) samples N=200 prompts from production-sampled store (with frequency weights), 3) runs both baseline and candidate models/configs via the local test runtime (or replay in canary), 4) computes per-field comparisons using field adapters (presence, numeric dist, token metrics), 5) aggregates into weighted metrics and stores a canonical JSON report in s3://redwood-evals/sample-weighted/<change_id>.json, 6) emits metrics to telemetry via metrics-api and creates an alerting event if thresholds exceeded.

Weighting: default weight = request_frequency * business_priority_score (from prompt metadata). Provide override to switch to uniform sampling for debugging.

Per-field adapters: implement a plugin interface so teams can add custom comparators for special fields (currency amounts, typed IDs). Keep default library minimal but cover strings, enums, arrays, nested objects.

Noise control: use bootstrapped confidence intervals on each metric and only surface fields with statistically-significant changes. Smooth by rolling 3-run median for alerts to reduce flapping.

Storage/Retention: keep full run artifacts 90 days; emit condensed index to Console for 365 days.

Privacy: redact PII from sample inputs and outputs before storage; use the same sanitizer utilities as incident recordings.

Backwards compatibility: the job supports comparing against a pinned baseline model version or the previous production commit.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for adapters and metric calculations (coverage >= 85%).
- Integration test: run job end-to-end against synthetic baseline and mutated-candidate models that introduce controlled regressions; verify alerts and JSON report fields.
- Canary rollout: enable on a single low-traffic route for 72 hours, validate alert false-positive rate < 5% on synthetic checks.
- Manual review: PM + SRE review of the first 10 runs and the alert payloads.
- Post-launch: run a retrospective after 2 weeks to tune thresholds and weights.
rollout_plan:
1) Prototype/Spike (week 1): implement adapters and run locally against replay data. 2) Internal dogfood (week 2): enable for infra routes and monitor. 3) Canaries (week 3): attach to canary rollouts for 3 customers. 4) Gradual enable (weeks 4-6): flip on for all rollouts behind a feature flag; expose alert opt-in in Console. 5) GA (week 8): default on for new rollouts with operator override.

Rollback: alerts do not change traffic; remediation actions suggested in the payload (rollback link to deployment). Emergency mute available via /api/v1/eval-alerts/mute for 24h.
